segments.text: The pravṛta, yadīturī rāsāvṣṭambena maddipādamsinjati, punāra-pītadā,
eva-meva previously what we have explained that this inferior way of generation of self
takes place to samyogīs, where they find experience the nature of self only in turya, not in
other states, not in other three states. This is our prasva, inferior generation of self.
Although this inferior generation of self has taken place pravṛta, eva-meva prasvape pravṛta,
when a yogi turya rāsāvṣṭambena maddipādamsinjati, again sprinkles the on and the rāsā of that
turya in other three states, then what happens to him? He explains this in next sutra, madra-soprṛta-yesandhane,
nāstrasya punar utthānam, madra-yin-objective world, that is utthānam, when coming out from samadhi.
A yogi, soprṛta-yesandhane, when a yogi tries to maintain awareness of God consciousness, in objective world also.
Then although nāstrasya, his real nature of self is destroyed by this inferior generation of self consciousness.
Punar utthānam, he gets again re-rises in that supreme nature of self. Punar utthānam.
Madrasu, madrasu means padarthesu in all these objective worlds.
And in this objective world, when soprṛta-yesandhane, he concentrates and becomes aware of his God consciousness.
Then he explains it in these two references.
Čekśa-yatsya-sandhānam, vācā-yatsya-ghojara, vācāvāyatsya-ghojara, manashchanti-yate-yani, buddhichaya-va-devastity.
Whatever is felt by form, by eyes, vācāvāyatsya-ghojara, whatever is felt by speech.
Manashchanti-yate-yani, whatever is felt by mind and whatever is perceived by intellect.
āhankrata-yani-yani, whatever is owned by ego, irainess, inferiority, i.e. of irainess.
Čekśa-yatsya-yatsya-yatsya-ghojara, and whatever is existing in objective world and whatever is not existing in objective world.
That is ākāsh-push-etc.
So tattrava-tannesh-tabya-prayatnā, that Supreme God consciousness should be sought with great effort in all these things.
Yajisri-sachandani-yate-yate-yata, this is explained in Sachandata-tantra.
And by this way, when Yogi Vishamidamaham, this whole universe is one with myself.
Yati-chit-ganātma-rupa-tām-sarvata-ansandata, and he meditates and perceives the fullness of God-consciousness in each and every object.
Then, purvokta-avara-prasavāt-nastaseva, the one that Yogi, whose God-consciousness was absolutely destroyed by that inferior way of generative consciousness,
inferior way of generation of that God-consciousness.
In other words, apahairita-turi-yate-chamad-kāramai-savāsa, whose nature was apaharita, apaharita removed, snatched away by that inferior way of trans.
To him, again, this puna-ru-tanam, puna-ru-tanam, again re-rise. He re-rises in his own nature.
In this way that tādhāike-sampat-sampur-natham-yoginā-bhavati, he becomes one with the glory of that God-consciousness, again.
It is said in Swachandha also, prasahie-sangjali-teva-yogināma-pianmana.
The mind of Yogi's is forcefully diverted towards worldly pleasures.
It is the way of energy of Maya, of God.
Although there are Yogi's also, to those Yogi's also, mind is forcefully diverted towards worldly pleasures and not God-consciousness.
But in those masses of Yogi's, some great Yogi who is fully aware of his self, yasi-gaya-yumayo-bhāva-sthera-purna-samandata,
whose that God-consciousness, the object of God-consciousness, is established, is full, and is all-round complete.
To him, mono-nur-chalitam tasya-sarva-bha-stha-gatasya, his mind never becomes diversion.
His mind never gets diversion.
Diversion towards worldly pleasures.
To for him, another thing happens to him.
Yatriyatra-mano-yati, wherever his mind flows out, gayam-tatra-vichinte-yati.
He centralizes his consciousness towards that one God-consciousness.
Chalita-yasi-te-kutra.
If his mind moves here and there still, it does not move at all.
It moves in his own nature, because he feels that everywhere is one-ness of Shiva, existing.
Vishisya-sarva-shu, Indriyārtha-jāstitam, Yatriyatra-yatra-nuru-peta-nashvam-vidita-kocitam.
Yatriyatra-nuru-peta, wherever he feels and experiences the existence of Objective World.
He feels that actually that Objective World is nothing but only Shiva.
